record.original_question: What is the absorption-dependent, imaginary part of the K− nuclear potential in normal nuclear matter, and how can pion-induced φ-meson and K− production measurements separate intrinsic in-medium φ-meson modifications from K− absorption behavior in nuclei?

evidence.quote: strangeness production in pion-induced reactions is well suited to study the kaon absorption in normal nuclear matter density.

On the other hand, in order to disentangle the intrinsic properties of the φ meson in the nucleus from the K− behavior, exclusive analysis can be carried out to tag the K− not coming from the φ decay.

The K− scattering length is known from kaonic atom experiments [2], while not very much is known on the absorption potential. The planned measurement should provide a valid contribution to determine the imaginary part of this potential.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the antikaon (K−) propagating in nuclear matter at normal saturation density ρ₀ ≈ 0.16 fm⁻³. Model the K−–nucleus interaction by a complex optical potential U(ρ) = V(ρ) + i W(ρ), where V is the real (dispersive) part and W is the imaginary (absorptive) part arising from inelastic channels such as K−N → πY (Y = Λ, Σ) and multi-nucleon absorption K−(NN) → YN. The real part is constrained near threshold by the K⁻–proton scattering length extracted from kaonic-hydrogen and kaonic-atom data, but the absorptive part W(ρ₀) at finite nuclear density is poorly determined.

(a) Determine the depth and density dependence of W(ρ) at ρ = ρ₀, that is, give a quantitative value (in MeV) of Im U(ρ₀) for a K− at rest (or at low momentum) in symmetric nuclear matter, including the relative weight of one-nucleon versus multi-nucleon absorption channels.

(b) Consider pion-induced reactions on nuclei of the form π⁻ A → φ X and π⁻ A → K⁺K⁻ X, in which a φ meson is produced and subsequently decays into a K⁺K⁻ pair inside the nuclear medium. Devise an exclusive analysis—based on kinematic tagging that distinguishes K− mesons originating from φ decay from K− mesons produced directly—that separates (i) intrinsic in-medium modifications of the φ meson (mass shift Δm_φ and width broadening Γ*_φ at density ρ₀) from (ii) the K− absorption properties encoded in W(ρ). Specify the observables (e.g., the A-dependence of the φ transparency ratio T_A = σ(πA→φX)/(A·σ(πN→φN)), the K− momentum spectrum, and the K⁺K⁻ invariant-mass distribution) and show how their combined measurement uniquely determines W(ρ₀), Δm_φ(ρ₀) and Γ*_φ(ρ₀).
artifact.status_search_result: The determination of the imaginary part of the K− nuclear optical potential at normal nuclear density and the disentangling of in-medium φ properties from K− final-state absorption remain active research topics in hadron–nuclear physics. Various theoretical estimates (chiral coupled-channel, phenomenological fits to kaonic atoms) yield W(ρ₀) ranging roughly from −40 to −100 MeV, but no consensus value is established, and dedicated pion-beam experiments (e.g., HADES, J-PARC E29-type proposals) are still needed for a definitive separation. No conclusive solution found.

status_evidence.title: Kaonic atoms and antikaon-nucleus interaction
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews uncertainties in the imaginary part of the K− optical potential extracted from kaonic-atom global fits, indicating significant model dependence.
status_evidence.claim: The absorptive part of the K− nuclear potential at ρ₀ remains model-dependent and not uniquely determined.

status_evidence.title: phi-meson in-medium properties and transparency ratio measurements
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ongoing efforts to extract intrinsic φ in-medium width separately from kaon final-state interactions via transparency ratios in pion- and proton-induced reactions.
status_evidence.claim: Separation of intrinsic φ modification from K− absorption is still an open experimental/theoretical task.
